# Volume 3 — Chapter XXXIII “He Just Kept Coming and Coming”

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

When Nell arrived back from school three days afterward, she discovered Thora weeping. Because tears and Thora appeared so ill-matched, Nell felt genuinely frightened.
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0000 }

“Oh, what is wrong?” she asked with great concern.
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0001 }

“Today I reach—I reach forty,” wept Thora.
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0002 }

“Indeed, you came close to that yesterday and remained unharmed,” offered Nell reassuringly, attempting to suppress a grin.
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0003 }

“However—however,” continued Thora, swallowing hard, “John Fairlie is not going to propose to me.”
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0004 }

“Oh, but he is going to,” Nell uttered weakly. “Thora, you have to allow him time
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0005 }

“Time!” Thora uttered, her voice dripping with unimaginable disdain. “Twenty years have been given to him. Exactly how much time is he asking for?”
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0006 }

“Are you saying that John Fairlie has visited you over a period of twenty years?”
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0007 }

“He has done so. And he has not once brought up the topic of marriage to me. Furthermore, I doubt he will at this point. I have never uttered a single word regarding this to any living soul, yet it feels as though I must finally discuss it with somebody or lose my mind. John Fairlie started courting me two decades ago, prior to mother's death. Well, his visits continued repeatedly, and following a period of time, I started sewing quilts and other items; however, he failed to ever mention marriage, merely continuing to visit over and over. I was completely helpless. Mother passed away after we had been courting for eight years. I anticipated that he might express his intentions at that time, considering I was left by myself in the world. He proved to be truly compassionate and empathetic, doing all he possibly could on my behalf, yet he never uttered the word marry. And that is precisely how things have proceeded up to the present. I am blamed for this by people. They claim that I refuse to marry him owing to his mother being so frail and my desire to avoid the trouble of caring for her. Why, taking care of John's mother would bring me joy! Nevertheless, I permit them to hold that belief. Having them blame me is preferable to having them pity me! The fact that John refuses to propose to me is so terribly embarrassing. And what is his motive for not doing so? It feels to me that if I simply understood his rationale, it would not bother me nearly as much.”
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0008 }

“It could be that his mother prefers he remains unmarried,” Nell offered.
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0009 }

“Oh, she does. Repeatedly, she has mentioned to me that she would be delighted to witness John established before she dies. She is constantly dropping hints to him—the other day, you listened to her yourself. My impression was that I would have dropped right through the floor.”
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0010 }

“It’s beyond me,” Nell admitted helplessly. Her thoughts turned to Ludovic Speed. The two situations, however, were not alike. John Fairlie differed greatly in character from Ludovic.
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0011 }

“Thora, you ought to display greater firmness,” she continued determinedly. “For what reason did you not dismiss him a long time since?”
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0012 }

“I wasn’t able to,” miserable Thora uttered mournfully. “The thing is, Nell, my affection for John has always been huge. Since no one else could ever be the one for me, his continued visits were perfectly fine, making it a non-issue.”
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0013 }

“Yet it could have compelled him to voice his thoughts like a man,” insisted Nell.
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0014 }

Thora gave a shake of her head.
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0015 }

“No, I suppose I do not. All the same, I was scared to attempt it, fearing he would believe I was serious and simply leave. I am likely a weak-willed person, yet that is my feeling. And I am unable to change it.”
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0016 }

“Oh, you were capable of preventing it, Thora. There is still time. Position yourself resolutely. Make that man understand that you will no longer tolerate his indecision. You will have my support.”
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0017 }

“I am not sure,” Thora stated in despair. “I am not sure whether I would ever be brave enough. The situation has been allowed to slide for a very long time. However, I am going to consider it.”
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0018 }

Nell believed that John Fairlie had let her down. She had held such a high opinion of him, never suspecting he was the kind of person who would toy with a woman’s affections for two decades. It was clear to her that he ought to be taught a lesson, and Nell harbored a vengeful desire to witness it happen. Consequently, she was thrilled when Thora informed her, while walking to prayer-meeting the following evening, that she intended to display some “sperrit.”
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0019 }

“I am going to make John Fairlie realize that he cannot walk all over me anymore.”
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0020 }

“You are entirely correct,” declared Nell with strong emphasis.
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0021 }

After the conclusion of the prayer-meeting, John Fairlie approached to make his customary plea. Thora appeared fearful yet determined.
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0022 }

“No, thank you,” she answered with an icy tone. “I am quite familiar with the way back on my own. It is only natural, given that I have been journeying along it for forty years. Therefore, you do not need to bother yourself, Mr. Fairlie.”
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0023 }

Nell’s eyes were fixed on John Fairlie; and, beneath that vivid moon, the final turn of the rack was visible to her once more. Silently, he swung around and marched away along the path.
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0024 }

“Stop! Stop!” Nell shouted frantically behind him, paying no attention whatsoever to the rest of the stunned spectators. “Mr. Fairlie, stop! Return.”
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0025 }

John Fairlie came to a halt, yet he refrained from returning. Nell rushed along the road, grabbed his arm, and practically pulled him back toward Thora.
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0026 }

“You have to return,” she begged. “This is entirely a error, Mr. Fairlie—the fault is all mine. I forced Thora to do it. She was unwilling—however everything is fine now, isn’t it, Thora?”
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0027 }

Thora grabbed his arm and departed silently. Submissively following them back to the house, Nell crept inside through the rear entrance.
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0028 }

“Indeed, you support me so wonderfully,” Thora uttered with sarcasm.
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0029 }

“Thora, I was helpless to prevent it,” Nell stated with remorse. “It simply seemed to me that I had passively witnessed a murder taking place. Running after him became my only choice.”
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0030 }

“Oh, I am equally pleased that you did so. As I watched John Fairlie departing along that road, it seemed to me that all the remaining joy and happiness in my life were departing alongside him. That feeling was terrible.”
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0031 }

“Was there any question from him about your reasons?” Nell inquired.
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0032 }

“No, he didn’t ever mention it,” Thora answered listlessly.
{: #nw-v03-c33-p0033 }
